cl_xc_mindset_before.q: Does how I feel beforehand change how a psychedelic trip goes?
cl_xc_mindset_before.short: Feeling calm and ready beforehand went with easier trips; feeling anxious went with more anxiety.
cl_xc_mindset_before.but: These are links: no study changed how people felt beforehand to test it.
how: About 650 people planning their own trip answered surveys before and after; about 200 answered enough to be counted.
Those who felt calm, open and ready the day before said the trip was less hard than others did.
In lab studies of LSD, feeling anxious before the dose went with more anxiety. Feeling well went with stronger effects overall, not easier ones.
Bigger links come from people remembering their mood afterwards, and memories can be coloured by how the trip went.

cl_xc_setting_support.q: Do the place and the people around me affect a trip?
cl_xc_setting_support.short: In surveys, feeling safe and supported went with fewer difficult moments, by small amounts.
cl_xc_setting_support.but: People rated this looking back; the one study that asked beforehand found only a weak link.
how: In a study that asked the day before, feeling good about the place and people went with slightly easier trips, but the link was weak and could be chance.
Among almost 7,000 people who drank ayahuasca, those who felt safer and better supported at the ceremony reported a little less fear than others.
In a US survey, people who blamed a lack of support for their hardest trip said it was harder than people who did not.
No study put people in different places on purpose to compare them.

cl_aya_ceremony_setting.q: Does the kind of ayahuasca ceremony matter for how it goes?
cl_aya_ceremony_setting.short: People who felt safe and supported at their last ceremony recalled a little less fear.
cl_aya_ceremony_setting.but: One survey: people rated the ceremony and how it went at the same time, looking back.
how: Almost 7,000 people who had drunk ayahuasca answered one online survey about their last ceremony.
Those who felt safer and better supported recalled a little less fear, and fewer problems in the weeks after, than those who felt less so.
More traditional practices, and drinking in Amazon countries other than Brazil, went with more fear; church hymns or sermons with less.
Fasting showed no link the study could detect with fear or later problems. All the differences were small, and nothing was measured before people drank.

cl_xc_difficult_how_common.q: How often are psychedelic trips difficult, and can problems last?
cl_xc_difficult_how_common.short: 41 in 100 people who had used psychedelics recalled at least one difficult trip.
cl_xc_difficult_how_common.but: One online survey, looking back over a whole life, using questions borrowed from meditation research.
how: 613 US adults who had ever used a psychedelic answered one online survey.
59 in 100 said they never had a difficult trip. About 5 in 100 said one badly affected their daily life, and 3 in 100 got help.
In the days or weeks after, 7 in 100 thought about or tried hurting themselves or others; 15 in 1,000 tried to harm themselves.
57 in 100 said worry, poor sleep or a similar problem lasted days, but people who had not used psychedelics were not asked.

freq.title: Out of every 100 people who had ever used a psychedelic, in one US online survey:
pairs: said they had had at least one difficult experience
said one had severely affected their ability to get through daily life
sought medical or psychological help afterwards
freq.note: 613 US adults asked once, in 2021, looking back over their whole life (251, 28 and 16 people). No one who had not used psychedelics was asked.
